newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO TO EXAMINE BIDS FOR 250,000 PHONE LINES.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO TO EXAMINE BIDS FOR 250,000 PHONE LINES.

text.p: Morocco will this week examine bids by foreign firms to expand by 250,000 lines its domestic telephone network, including GSM mobile phones, a Moroccan official said on Monday.

"The state-owned Office National des Postes et Telecommunications (ONPT) will examine this week offers made by international telephone firms to expand Morocco's network by an extra 250,000 lines," said the official, who declined to be named.
The date when the winner of the tender, which was launched earlier this year, would be announced was not known, he added.
The tender coincided with the adoption by parliament of a law on liberalising the sector ahead of its partial privatisation.
The liberalisation programme aims to split the ONPT utility into two enterprises called Ittissalat al-Maghrib and Barid al-Maghrib, handling respectively telecommunications and postal services.
Privatisation will first target GSM phones.

In line with the liberalisation strategy, the ONPT also cut tariffs by up to 25 percent for international calls and reduced some charges for access to GSM mobile phones, an analyst at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities said.
South Korean giant Daewoo, the U.S. AT&T and French Alcatel companies have all closely followed the moves towards telecoms liberalisation, he said.
Daewoo has said it would invest up to 1.0 billion dirhams ($105 million) in the GSM network in Morocco after its privatisation, the broker added.
Morocco with a population of 27 million people has only four telephone lines per 100 people and an estimated 50,000 GSM subscribers.
